newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE AND HASTINGS DROPPED, CARLING RETAINED.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE AND HASTINGS DROPPED, CARLING RETAINED.

text.p: David Campese was sadly if predictably dropped on Wednesday from the Australian side to meet Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday.
The world record try scorer, who won his 100th cap against Italy last month, was replaced by Joe Roff in the Wallaby lineup.
Campese, 34, is still in magnificent condition thanks to a rigorous training schedule he has pursued since his international debut 14 years ago.
But although he retains his flair for the unexpected his speed has gone and the famous goose-step is now executed in slow motion.
Campese appears doomed to play a bit part on the Wallabies' tour of Britain and Ireland with a likely farewell in the Australian colours against the Barbarians at Twickenham on December 7.

Scott Hastings, Scotland's leading international cap, is also missing from the lineup for Saturday with captain Gregor Townsend, their best player in last season's Five Nations' championship, switching from fly-half to the centres.
Craig Chalmers has been recalled at fly-half to renew his partnership with Gary Armstrong.
"Craig's play has changed completely since this time last year," said Scotland backs' coach David Johnston. "Playing him at stand-off will give us good options."
South of the border there was an unexpected reprieve for former England captain Will Carling for the international against Italy on November 23.
Carling looked destined for a spot on the replacements' bench and effective retirement from international rugby after Phil de Glanville was named as England captain on Tuesday.
But in a surprise move England manager Jack Rowell omitted Jeremy Guscott and teamed Carling and de Glanville in the centres.

"As soon as Phil de Glanville was named captain, the centre positions were always going to be a difficult selection," Guscott said. "Both Will and I are playing well, so I will just have to accept the decision gracefully."
Rowell now effectively has two inside centres outside Mike Catt who moves from full-back to fly-half and will assume the goal-kicking duties.
